# WAAAGH! MAGIC

*Pages PDF 94-101*

## ## Waaagh! Magic
Orcs and Goblins do not distinguish between magic and religion. As far as they are concerned, their Shamans wield uncanny energies given to them by their gods, the cunning but brutal Mork and the brutal but cunning Gork. Orcs and Goblins are not known for their philosophical musings — they don’t question why or how their gods provide such sorcery, they just accept that’s the way of the world… and enjoy the carnage. 

According to wizards in Altdorf ’s Colleges of Magic, the magic of Orcs and Goblins isn’t powered solely by the Winds of Magic. It seems the power for Shaman’s spells arise from the collective raw energy of a mob of Orcs or Goblins, hence it is often called ‘Waaagh! Magic’. The more excited, numerous, and aggressive a group of Orcs, the greater the power emanating from the crowd. During a fight or battle, this energy crackles from the chanting Orcs and Goblins and finds a conduit through the Shamans, who wrestle to shape it into spells. These magical displays are as boisterous and violent as Orcs themselves — very few Shamans invoke the subtle magics practiced by other species. 

Shamans are an unusual caste amongst Orc and Goblin tribes. They are prone to peculiar, eccentric behaviour, which becomes even more bizarre as Waaagh! energy leaves their minds increasingly unhinged. Bosses know it’s useful to have a Shaman around. They’re great in a fight and they help keep the gods sweet — but there’s something not right about them. 

Other Orcs and Goblins are unnerved by the sheer weirdness of a Shaman, not to mention the coloured lights playing around their head as they mutter, howl, and caper about the place. It doesn’t help that they have a tendency to explode when they lose control of the vast energies coursing through their bodies. 

## **Orc and Goblin Spellcasting**
Greenskin Shamans are as diverse as their tribes and species — each one is a uniquely strange individual. Every Shaman has their own repertoire of peculiar rituals and dances, some of their own invention, others picked up from fellow Shamans. Their spells are similar… cobbled together from instinct, mimicry, and divine inspiration. 

Their spellcasters use magic rules from the rulebook, with the following additions: 

- Orc and Goblin Shamans draw power from the Waaagh! — the psychic energy of massed Orcs and Goblins. 

- Provided there are Orcs and Goblins in the general vicinity, the Shaman may make Channelling and Casting Tests as usual and may benefit from tools such as Staffs or other magic items. 

- If the Shaman is isolated from other Orcs and Goblins (meaning that there are no such creatures visible to it, and that the population is scarce in the surrounding environment) they suffer –2 SL to any Channelling or Casting Tests. 

- When Channelling, the Shaman benefits by +1 SL for every Orc, Hobgoblin, and 2 Goblins within Willpower yards. 

- However, if a miscast occurs, use the Waaagh! Miscast Table on page 96 rather than the Major or Minor Miscast Tables, and add 2 to the result for every Orc, Hobgoblin, and 2 Goblins within Willpower Bonus yards. 

## **Orcs**
Orc Shamans are ostracised by most bosses, who would rather they prance about somewhere out of sight. Their spells are brutal, bludgeoning affairs — all Orc Shamans have the _Arcane Magic (Big Waaagh!)_ Talent. 

## **Savage Orcs**
Savage Orcs hold Shamans in high regard, as embodiments of elemental Orciness free from the taint of modernity. Their Shamans indulge in much chanting, drumming, and waving their arms about. Savage Orc Shamans have the _Arcane Magic (Big Waaagh!)_ Talent. 

Their attire varies greatly — for example, Shamans from the hills and plains wear furs and skulls, while bogdwelling Goblins drape themselves in stinking weeds and frog skins. 

Goblin Shamans have the _Arcane Magic (Little Waaagh!)_ Talent. 

## **Night Goblins**
Night Goblin Shamans are attuned to the strange mystical fungi crucial to life beneath the mountains. They have secret knowledge for cultivating the madcap mushroom and shaman shrooms used in tribal rituals. 

## **Goblins**
Goblin Shamans like to scare their fellows with magic to keep themselves high in the tribal pecking order. They claim to channel Mork and Gork, along with other spirits and minor deities associated with their tribe. 

Night Goblin Shamans have the _Arcane Magic (Little Waaagh!)_ Talent. Shaman Shrooms and their effects are described on page 99. 

## **Forest Goblins**
Forest Goblin Shamans commune with the Feaster from Beyond, their Great Spider-God, and cast spells with a hairy, eight-legged flavour. Spiders crawl across their spindly bodies, their bites inducing mystical trances. The Purple Skullback is especially potent, its bite granting vivid visions of the Feaster’s cobwebbed realm. 

Forest Goblin Shamans have the _Arcane Magic (Little Waaagh!)_ Talent. The Purple Skullback and its effects are described on page 99. 

## **Hobgoblins**
Hobgoblin Shamans are very rarely seen west of the Mountains of Mourn. They shuffle around, hunched over from countless thick furs draped across their backs. Many carry and wear fearsome masks that represent the wicked steppe spirits, Mork-khan, and Gork-khan. 

Hobgoblin Shamans can have either the _Arcane Magic (Big Waaagh!)_ or _(Little Waaagh!)_ Talents. Shaman Lords can have both, but may take no more than two spells from one of the Talents.

## **Orc and Goblin Magic Items**
Orcs and Goblins are not great artificers and do not understand the principles of magic in a disciplined sense. They do make magical items, imbuing them with Waaagh! energy, but the results are crude and unpredictable. 

## **Copper Staff**
Some of the more cunning and cautious Shamans have discovered that copper provides a suitable vector for excess Waaagh! energy. Whilst holding the staff, they count as isolated from other Orcs and Goblins (with a –2 SL penalty to Channelling or Casting Tests) and they ignore the presence of Orcs, Hobgoblins, and Goblins when rolling on the Waaagh! Miscast Table. 

## **Dangly Wotnotz**
Many Orc and Goblin Shamans wear bangles and pendants bedecked with bones, teeth, and petty fetishes. These items are imbued with Waaagh! power and help regulate the magical power gathered by the Shaman for the purpose of working magic. A Shaman in possession of Dangly Wotnotz may reroll a successful Casting Test in the hope of getting a better result if they wish. They must accept the results of the second roll. 

## **Effigy of Mork**
Formed from dried and enchanted Orc dung, the Effigy of Mork provides a Shaman with insights into how to avoid the blows of his enemies. A Shaman in possession of an Effigy of Mork may reroll any Dodge Tests or Melee Tests made to oppose an attack. The results of the rerolled test must stand as the final result, even if they produce worse consequences for the Shaman. 

## **Effigy of Gork**
The Effigy of Gork provides insights into how to inflict harm. A Shaman in possession of an Effigy of Gork may reroll any Melee Tests made to attack an opponent. The results of the rerolled test must stand as the final result, even if they produce worse consequences for the Shaman. 

## **Glowy Green Amulet**
This small and unobtrusive amulet grows with green power every time the wearer is made the target of a hostile spell. The enchantment upon the amulet is powerful but unstable. The bearer is granted the Magic Resistance 2 Talent. However, every time the bearer is targeted by a spell roll 1d100. On the result of a 01 the amulet violently vents its energies. The Shaman suffers 1d10 Wounds (ignore TB and Armour) and the _Prone_ Condition. 

## **Shaman Staff**
The most common magic item possessed by a Shaman is a staff adorned with all manner of gruesome trophies and shiny trinkets. These staffs attract Waaagh! energy even when other Orcs and Goblins are nowhere to be seen. Roll 1d10 for any given staff. The Shaman always counts as being within Willpower Bonus yards of this many Orcs when Channelling, Casting, or rolling on the Waaagh! Miscast Table. 

## Research and Orc and Goblin Magical Items
Orcs and Goblins employ designs of magical artefacts that do not derive energy from the Winds of Magic, but the Waaagh! energy derived from the innate nature of Orcs, Goblins, and related creatures. If a Witch, Wizard, or other sort of magic user wishes to learn an Orc spell or employ a magic item that uses Waaagh! energy, they are embarking on a very dangerous course of action. 

Exactly how this risk manifests is left up to the GM, but any investigation of an Orc or Goblin artefact ought to be an exacting process where any missteps result not only in corruption exposure, but also judicious use of the Waaagh! Miscasts Table. 

## **Spells of the Little Waaagh!**
The spells of Goblin (and some Hobgoblin) Shamans tend to manifest the Waaagh! as spiteful tricks and hexes. Goblin Shamans grow in confidence as their spells work. If they generate any SL on their Casting Tests, they may spend it on Overcasting or may use it to buy a single Fortune Point. Fortune Points earned in this way can take the Shaman’s normal Fortune above it’s maximum, but must be spent by the end of the encounter, or are lost.

## Shaman Shrooms
Shaman Shrooms are mushrooms that have sprouted from the bodies of Night Goblin Shamans. The process is selfsustaining, for the more Shaman Shrooms a Night Goblin Shaman consumes, the more likely he is to become infested with fungi, and then perish to produce more Shaman Shroom in turn. 

Despite the risk, the consumption of Shaman Shrooms by Night Goblin Shamans is common practice, as they grant the Shaman a powerful infusion of Waaagh! energy. A Shaman may eat a piece of Shaman Shroom as an Action. For the next 2d10 Rounds, they make Channelling Tests and Casting Tests as if there are 2d10 additional Goblins within Willpower Bonus yards. However, they also must also add this number to any results they score on the Waaagh! Miscast Table. 

## **Duration:** Instant
The Shaman conjures up a pair of green hands. He may attempt to pick the pocket of any target in range as if he were possessed of a Sleight of Hand skill of 55. If the attempt is successful, the target may make a **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test to notice the hands (and loot) flying back to the Shaman.

Shaman Shrooms may also influence the result of the Waaagh! Miscast Table if the Shroom Spurt result is unfortunate enough to occur.

**Traits:** Arboreal, Night Vision, Size (Tiny), Venom (Challenging), Wallcrawler, Weapon (Fangs) +2 

**Bite of the Purple Skullback:** If a Character suffers from a Wound and subsequently takes a _Poisoned_ Condition as a result of a bite by a Purple Skullback, they must pass an **Average (+20) Cool** Test or gain 1 Corruption point as they are haunted by disturbing magical hallucinations. 

Forest Goblin Shamans are an exception to this. When they are bitten by a Purple Skullback, they must still take damage and test to avoid being poisoned, but whether or not they gain a _Poisoned_ Condition, their connection to the realm of the Spider-God grants them heightened magical abilities. For the next 2d10 hours, the Shaman benefits from an additional 2d10 bonus to their Channelling Skill and Language (Magick) Skill. 

During this time, the Shaman may also reroll any results they generate on the Waaagh! Miscast Table. 

## **Spells of the Big Waaagh!**
Orc and some Hobgoblin Shamans know an array of crude Orc magic. A selection of their repertoire is provided here. Spells of the Big Waaagh! act as conduits for massive ammounts of Waaagh! energy, and its release emboldens the hearts of nearby Orcs, Goblins, and Hobgoblins. Whenever a Character casts a spell of the Big Waaagh! any Orcs, Hobgoblins, or Goblins within Willpower yards lose any _Broken_ Conditions.

## Idols of Gork and Mork
Orcs and Goblins are known for raising great idols to their gods to mark the edges of their territory and their bases of operations. These idols come in a variety of designs. Some are formed from piles of rocks with wooden masks, others are simple wattle-and-daub frames piled high with reeking dung, and others are formed from the defaced statues of Human heroes or Dwarf ancestors. These idols are all rough and crude in their construction, but all of them depict a titanic Orc, belligerent and mighty. 

**Target:** See Text 

**Duration:** Willpower Bonus Rounds 

The Shaman conjures an enormous ethereal green hand which scoops up 1d10 targets and plonks them down somewhere within range. Targets must be within Willpower Bonus yards of one another. On landing, they gain +1 Advantage in combat if they enter Melee immediately. If using Group Advantage add Advantage points to the Orc and Goblin pool equal to the number of targets. 

## **Mork Save Us!**
These idols draw in Waaagh! energy and act as a battery of magical power, in much the same way as certain waystones and ley lines (see **Winds of Magic** for more details). An Orc or Goblin Shaman who is within Willpower Yards of an Idol of Gork or Mork may benefit from +1 SL to any Casting and Channelling Tests they make. If the idol is specifically of Mork, then spells cast from the Lore of the Little Waaagh! benefit from an additional +1 SL provided they are successfully cast, and if the idol is specifically of Gork, then spells cast from the Lore of the Big Waaagh! benefit from an additional +1 SL provided they are successfully cast. 

## **Cn:** 8
**Range:** Willpower Bonus yards 

**Target:** See Text 

**Duration:** Willpower Bonus Rounds 

The Shaman beseeches Mork to provide protection to his allies. For every SL scored on the casting roll, the Shaman may imbue an allied Orc, Goblin, or Hobgoblin within range with the _Ward 10_ Creature Trait. If the target already has a _Ward_ Trait, the rating is improved by 1. A _Ward_ Trait may not be improved to 7+ or better in this manner. 

On rare occasions, an Idol of Gork or Mork may become so infused with Waaagh! energy that it becomes animate and rampages around. The rules for constructs given in **Winds of Magic** could be used to create a Rogue Idol of this sort.
